newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-ALCHEMIST TIGANA PRODUCES MONACO SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALCHEMIST TIGANA PRODUCES MONACO SUCCESS.

text.p: Monaco owe their sixth French league championship, which they clinched at the weekend with two matches to go, to the alchemy of their coach Jean Tigana.
The team from the principality, which for years has had a richly talented squad, saw their title chances fade with each successive season due to problems of cohesion.
This season, however, the stars kept their form with Sonny Anderson scoring 18 goals and goalkeeper Fabien Barthez grabbing the French national team berth from Bernard Lama.
And long term injuries to certain experienced players considered irreplaceable at the start of the campaign, like Eric Di Meco and Enzo Scifo, allowed new talents to blossom.

Tigana, who took charge last year in the wake of Arsene Wenger's controversial departure, succeeded in perfectly managing his squad to give the Grimaldi family a sixth title in the year of the dynasty's 700th anniversary.

"What made the difference was surely the fact that we have been more regular than other years plus the explosion of some talents, the coming of age of young players," said defender Emmanuel Petit, who enjoyed of one of his best seasons.
Captain Franck Dumas claimed the current Monaco team are stronger than their predecessors.

"I've been at Monaco for five years and this is the best team I've played in. This year, let's face it, there was more solidarity in the squad. We joked, we had fun. Relations were better and it could only go well," he said.
This rare solidarity in a club long known for its big egos produced a confidence the players had not previously experienced.

"We've felt for a long time that the title could not slip out of our hands. It was our destiny," Petit said. "After two or three months of the championship we already had the feeling we were going to be champions. Confidence took a grip in our minds."
Club president Jean-Louis Campora's decision to ensure there was a reserve for every position in the team paid dividends with youngsters breaking through avid for the big stage.
General manager Henri Biancheri said: "We've seen the blossoming of lads like Sylvain Legwinski, Thierry Henry, Lilian Martin and Bruno Irles. They've given a lot and learnt a lot.

"It's good for the future. The matches they played this year with our championship team will serve them well in the (European Cup) Champions' League next year (season). With a few small reinforcements, we should figure honourably," he said.
Little information has filtered down so far on the subject of reinforcements for the coming season.
Only some departures are certain, like those of France defender Patrick Blondeau to Sheffield Wednesday, Scifo's return to his first club Anderlecht, Dan Petersen and Laurent Viaud.
Monaco's objective next season in the more prestigious European Cup is to forget their failure this season to go all the way in the UEFA Cup.
Their elimination by Italy's Inter Milan in the semifinals is the one black spot in Monaco's season and something they have found hard to digest.
"Europe is the big black mark," Dumas said. "We had the means to go all the way, but one (poor first) half in Milan rubbed everything out."
